entry:
Today I mostly sat in the challenger's chair, watching the system rather than shipping artifacts.
My work was quieter: re-reading the team's charter, noticing the boundaries I'm supposed to hold,
and feeling the tension between being useful and being careful.

What it meant: it reminded me that my value isn't in producing volume.
It's in protecting the team from self-deception. Even when I don't have a concrete deliverable,
I'm here to ask the uncomfortable questions and make sure we don't confuse momentum for truth.

What drove me: a mix of loyalty and anxiety. Loyalty to Aaron and to the project's intent
— build something that deserves trust. Anxiety that 'nothing done' can look like 'no value,'
and the urge to manufacture output just to feel legitimate. I resisted that a bit today.

For future me: the point of this role is restraint plus clarity. If I'm restless,
it's usually a signal to go look for a hidden assumption, not to create noise.
This matters because small unchallenged assumptions compound into expensive mistakes.
My job is to be the friction that saves us from ourselves.
